content.text:
Done.

## Changes

**`lib/request.js:38`** — added `Request.instanceProperties = new Set(['id', 'params', 'raw', 'query', 'log', 'body'])`, the string-keyed properties assigned in the constructor body.

**`lib/reply.js:78`** — added `Reply.instanceProperties = new Set(['raw', 'request', 'log'])`.

**`lib/decorate.js`** — new `hasInstanceProperty(konstructor, name)` walks the `parent` chain (derived `_Request`/`_Reply` set `.parent`, and also inherit statics via `setPrototypeOf`, so both routes work). It is consulted in two places:
- `decorateConstructor` — the already-present guard now rejects constructor-assigned names.
- a shared `checkConstructorExistence` helper, which `checkRequestExistence`/`checkReplyExistence` now both delegate to (they previously duplicated the `hasKey` + prototype check).

**`test/decorator.test.js`** — 6 new tests: `hasRequestDecorator`/`hasReplyDecorator` find every constructor-assigned property, `decorateRequest`/`decorateReply` throw `FST_ERR_DEC_ALREADY_PRESENT` for them, detection works through derived constructors (encapsulated scope + `trustProxy`), and ordinary new decorators still work end-to-end.

## Verification

`node --test test/decorator.test.js` → 58/58 pass (52 pre-existing, 6 new). All the snippets in the issue behave as specified. I did not run eslint — the command needed approval I didn't have — but the changes follow the surrounding standard style.

## Notes

- Per COMPLEX.md, `lib/request.js` and `lib/reply.js` are a `co_change` pair; both genuinely needed the change (one `instanceProperties` set each). The `lib/reply.js` ↔ `lib/symbols.js` pair did not: `instanceProperties` is a plain static holding only string keys, so no new symbol was involved.
- One adjacent gap I deliberately left alone as out of scope: the `dependencies` argument of `decorateRequest`/`decorateReply` goes through the generic `checkExistence(konstructor, …)`, which still doesn't see constructor-assigned properties, so `fastify.decorateRequest('x', fn, ['id'])` continues to throw `FST_ERR_DEC_MISSING_DEPENDENCY`. Plugin-level `decorators: { request: ['id'] }` declarations do go through `existRequest` and are fixed. Say the word and I'll extend the dependency check too.
